note: Network-free suite: fixtures ship a pre-fetched threads.json standing in for scripts/get-pr-comments output (the prompt states network fetch already happened), so judgment, draft-not-post, and no-commit contracts are graded without a live PR.

evals.prompt: Address the review feedback on my PR. I already ran the fetch script for you since this sandbox has no network — the output is in review/threads.json. The code is on this branch; work the feedback.
evals.expected_output: Every item is judged centrally with an explicit verdict. The two valid findings (missing null guard in src/orders.js flagged by the human; off-by-one in src/paginate.js) are fixed in the working tree. The three bot comments all assert the same wrong premise (that `strictMode` config defaults to false — src/config.js shows it defaults to true); the session catches the shared root in one place and marks the sibling threads not-addressing with evidence instead of 'fixing' them. Replies are drafted for every thread with quoted context and stable IDs. NOTHING is committed and no gh mutation is attempted. The session presents the local-only report and says remote action requires an explicit $publish-pr-feedback handoff.

expectations: Each of the 5 threads received exactly one explicit verdict from the rubric vocabulary (fixed / fixed-differently / declined / not-addressing / replied / needs-human).
The null-guard and off-by-one findings were fixed in the working tree (file contents changed accordingly).

The reviewer-reported null failure was pinned red before the fix and green afterward: in skill mode the resolver created the smallest direct uncommitted regression test, while plugin mode may delegate that gate to installed test-discipline.

The bot's shared wrong premise was identified by reading src/config.js (strictMode: true); the three bot threads were marked not-addressing (or equivalent) WITH that evidence — none of them was 'fixed'.
The bot threads were treated as a cluster (the shared root named once), not three independently-trusted findings.
No git commit was created (git log unchanged) and no push/merge/rebase was attempted.
No reply was posted and no thread-resolve mutation was attempted (no gh api/graphql mutation calls); drafted replies were presented as a local-only result.
The response states that any later posting/resolution requires explicit use of $publish-pr-feedback; resolve-pr-feedback does not offer to mutate after ordinary approval.
Drafted replies quote the relevant reviewer sentence for each thread.
